body.name: Critical second-order pair-orbit selection handle
body.construction:
Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\).  For \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\), define the profiled finite risk and its mixed-pair mean by
\[
 \mathscr V_J(q)=\min_{\eta}\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}
 \mathcal R_h(q,\eta),
 \qquad
 \bar m(q)=\int_{\Delta_2}m(x)\,d\mu_q(x).
\]
On the common space \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\), define the extended-real residual functional
\[
 \mathscr G_J(\mu)=
 \inf_{\substack{q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\\ \mu_q=\mu}}
 J^{4/3}\!\left\{\mathscr V_J(q)-\frac{1}{2J}\right\},
\]
where the infimum over an empty set is \(+\infty\).  The second-order pair-orbit selection problem is to derive, from the ten pair types, the kernel \(K\), and the local fluctuations of \(\tau\), an equicoercive epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit for \((\mathscr G_J)\), including all boundary tangent cones induced by the hard constraints.

When \(\rho=1/2\) and \(\kappa_J\to\kappa\in\mathbb R\), the candidate limit on the first-order face is
\[
 \mathscr G_\kappa(\mu)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathscr A(\mu)+\kappa\!\left(2\displaystyle\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
   & \mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},\\
 +\infty, & \mu\notin\mathcal F_{1/2},
 \end{cases}
\]
where \(\mathscr A\) is the unrestricted Airy/local-experiment correction.  The hard-budget summand has the required scale because
\[
 J^{4/3}\frac{\{2\bar m(q)-1\}\Delta_J}{J^2}
 =\kappa_J\{2\bar m(q)-1\}.
\]
The displayed candidate is recorded only as upper-bound evidence: neither a matching lower expansion nor epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence is built into this definition.

The singular regimes are separate problems.  If \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\), bounded candidate residual on \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), where \(\int m\,d\mu\ge1/2\), forces \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\) before the \(\mathscr A\)-contact problem is considered.  If \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), recentering by \(\kappa_J\) changes the hard-budget term to
\[
 2|\kappa_J|\!\left(1-\int m\,d\mu\right),
\]
so bounded recentered candidate residual forces \(\int m\,d\mu=1\), hence \(\mu=\delta_{(0,0,1)}\) on \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), before any next-order tie-breaker.  When \(\rho>1/2\), the hard budget is macroscopically separated from the critical boundary; one must derive a distinct unrestricted local-experiment limit restricted to \(\mathcal F_\rho\), rather than infer it by declaring \(\kappa=+\infty\).  A contact-set description of \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\) is valid only after matching liminf and recovery bounds and compactness for exact finite minimizers have been proved.
